_doc: Where a reader marked Frances Glessner's facial landmarks on the 1892 conservatory photograph, in pixels of the crop `crop_px` (left, top, right, bottom) of the copy the owner supplied. Her face is about 90 px across in it, under half the scale of her husband's plate, so the marks carry about two-thirds of his uncertainties in pixels for the same share of the face. `sigma_px` is the reader's own uncertainty: the pupils are the irises' dark centres; the far eye's outer corner is near the cheek's outline; the nose tip is the highlight where the bridge turns under; the chin's lower edge meets the shadow above her ruff; the ear is her right, at the reader's left, with its top under the drawn-back hair. The crown is under her hair and is not marked. `base_body` fits against her own body's rest face (a woman's), not the kit's men's base. tools/fit_portrait_face.py fits the face to these marks.
age_note: The photograph is dated 4 March 1892 by the museum's record; born in 1848, she was 44. It is fitted as her face's shape: the renderer's ageing pair takes her to 56 at the scene date, as it does for every face.
basis: Fitted to a photograph of her showing her whole face (the Chicago History Museum's 1892 conservatory photograph, ICHi-061818): the eye spacing, nose, mouth, chin and ear placement are read from it, against her own body's face, as far as the shared MakeHuman face axes can express them. Depth is read from a single three-quarter view, so an axis the marks say little about stays near her body's own (listed as mostly_prior). Her 1897 multigraph (five views at once, two in profile) is held as a cross-check, not fitted: its heads are too small in the copy held. Her full cheeks, jowl, broad jaw and nose's breadth are read by eye from the photograph (read_by_eye), not measured.
not_modelled: her colouring (the photographs are monochrome; skin and hair colours are chosen)
her hair as she wore it (drawn up to a crown of braids in 1897; the model wears the town's bun)

card._doc: What the person's card shows (T-3473, as T-3413 for her husband): `portrait` is cut from the copy at `portrait_from_scan_px` (left, top, right, bottom) and scaled to `size_px`; `model` is tools/portrait_still.mjs's render of the fitted face on `body`, turned to the fit's yaw and framed like the portrait, dressed as humans.js dresses her in town. `hide` leaves out her hat and its plumes: the photograph is bareheaded.

read_by_eye.basis: Read by eye from the same photograph, on axes the marks cannot measure from one three-quarter view (owner, 2026-11-07: "frances looks young to me compared to the photo"): a broad, full face, its cheeks full below the cheekbones with no hollow under them, a heavy jaw line and the start of a jowl at 44, a nose broad at its wings, the eyes set under a fuller brow, and the corners of the mouth level to a little down at rest, not turned up. These replace the women's body's own young lean (narrow jaw, high cheekbones, flat brow, no jowl, a resting smile) as the prior on those axes; the marks still move them where they can.
